name: SikaGrout Deep Pour
paste:
SIKAGROUT® DEEP POUR: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaGrout® Deep Pour, May 2024, Version 01.05 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/u/sikagrout-deep-pour.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaGrout® Deep Pour where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2024, Version 01.05).
1.2 Product description.
    - SikaGrout®-Deep Pour is a ready mixed, high quality, Portland cement grout that expands in two stages (Class A and C), to counteract the shrinkage normally associated with Portland cement grouts.
    - SikaGrout® Deep Pour is a blend of Portland cement, carefully selected and graded aggregates and Sika Admixtures, enabling it to achieve high strengths in short times, making SikaGrout® Deep Pour suitable for grouting of large sections and deep pours of up to 500mm.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Mass grouting/concreting
    - Machine bedplates
    - Anchor bolts.
    - Bridge bearing pads.
    - Pre-cast concrete sections.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaGrout® Deep Pour
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: FLOWABLE, PRECISION CEMENTITIOUS GROUT FOR DEEP POURS UP TO 500 MM
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports.
    - Qld Roads (TMR) Section 5. Registered and Conforming Products. Part 5.3 Repair Grouts
    - RTA Rapid Mortar Bar Test (RTA T363) - Alkali Reactive Particles (Non-Reactive).
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS 1478.2: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Features (p.1).
    - EN 1015-17: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Soluble chloride ion content (p.1).
    - AS 1478.2:2005: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Flowability (p.2); Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.2).
    - AS 1012.10:2000: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Splitting tensile strength (p.2).
    - AS 2350.4:2006: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Setting time (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shrinkage compensating properties,
    - High early strengths.
    - High 28 day strengths.
    - Good flow characteristics.
    - Adjustable consistency.
    - Good impact and thermal resistance.
    - Non corrosive to steel or iron.
    - Lab tested in accordance with AS 1478.2
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Cement, selected aggregates and special additives
    - Appearance and colour: Grey powder
    - Density: ~ 2,300 kg/m³Fresh mortar density
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Maximum grain size: Dmax: 4.0 mm
    - Soluble chloride ion content: ≤ 0.05% (EN 1015-17)
2.7 Compressive strength.
    | 1 day | ~ 12.0 MPa |
    | 3 days | ~ 30.0 MPa |
    | 7 days | ~ 50.0 MPa |
    | 28 days | ~ 70.0 MPa |
    Test method printed: (AS 1478.2:2005)
    Note printed: Material and curing conditions at 23°C / 50% r.h. Above results based on 50x50mm cube specimens
2.8 Splitting tensile strength.
    | 28 days | ~ 5.0 MPa |
    Test method printed: (AS 1012.10:2000)
2.9 Electrical resistivity.
    | 7 days | ~ 14,000 Ω.cm |
    | 28 days | ~ 39,000 Ω.cm |
    | 56 days | ~ 53,000 Ω.cm |
    | 90 days | ~ 64,000 Ω.cm |
    Test method printed: (FM5-578)
    Note printed: 50mm Probe Spacing
2.10 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 20 kg bags
    - Shelf life: 9 months
    - Storage conditions: Store properly in undamaged original sealed packaging, in dry cool conditions.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2024, Version 01.05) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment.
    - Concrete
    - Correct and thorough surface preparation is essential to achieve the high performance qualities of SikaGrout® Deep Pour.
    - All surfaces must be clean, sound and free from dust, ice, oils, grease or other surface contaminants such as curing membranes and form release agent etc. Bolt holes and fixing pockets should be free of dirt and debris by air blasting. For maximum bond, surfaces should be abraded or roughened, preferably by mechanical means such as needle gun, grit blasting, grinding etc.
    - All prepared surfaces must be saturated with water several hours prior to grouting, ensuring it is free of any surface water or puddles.
    - Formwork
    - Where formwork is to be used, all formwork must be of adequate strength, treated with release agent and sealed to prevent leakage of pre-wetting water and grout. Ensure formwork includes outlets for removal of the pre-soaking water if vacuum extraction equipment to remove water will not be used. For manual grout application, a header box or hopper must be constructed on one side of the formwork so that a grout head can be maintained during the grouting operation.
    - Temperature control
    - Temperature affects setting time and rate of increase for strength. For optimum performance maintain grout, concrete and/or steel substrates within the range of 18-25 °C prior to, during, and for 48 hours after placement of the grout. At low temperatures (below 10 °C) grout setting time is extended and bleeding may occur. As a result, base plate contact may be reduced. To reduce the setting time of SikaGrout-Deep Pour, accelerating admixtures such as Sika-4A or Sika Rapid-1 may be added. At high temperatures (greater than 30 °C) grout setting time is reduced, affecting placement. It is recommended that grouting at high temperatures be sheltered from the heat, or be conducted early in the morning.
    - It is good practice to keep materials cool in high temperatures using cold water for mixing. Setting times can also be increased using a retarding admixture such as SikaTard-930. It is suggested that site trials be conducted to determine optimum dosage rates for recommended admixtures. For further details contact Sika’s Technical Department.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2024, Version 01.05) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Consumption: Approximately 102 bags per 1m³
    - Yield: 20 kg of powder yields approximately 9.8 litres of grout
    - Layer thickness: min. 20 mm / max. 500 mm
    - Flowability: ~ 500 mm (Flow trough) (AS 1478.2:2005)
    - Mixing ratio: 2.5 - 2.8 litres of water for 20kg powder
    - Pot Life: ~30 minutes at +20°C
4.3 Setting time.
    | Temperature | Initial Set | Final Set |
    | 23ºC | ~ 4 hrs 40 mins | ~ 7 hrs 45 mins |
    Test method printed: (AS 2350.4:2006)
4.4 Mixing.
    - SikaGrout® Deep Pour must be mechanically mixed using a mechanical grout mixer and suitable mixing container. It is recommended to mix a full bag in clean container using an electric drill / spiral drill and spiral mixer at a speed of approximately 500 rpm.
    - Pour the correct amount of water into a suitable clean mixing container. While stirring slowly with drill and spiral mixer, add the complete bag of powder into the water. Mix continuously for 3-5 minutes to achieve a uniform and lump free smooth consistency.
    - Do not add more water than the maximum specified.
4.5 Application. SikaGrout® Deep Pour can be placed by gravity flow or by pump. It is essential that proper placing on the job site is practised to ensure placement is completed without problems. Sufficient labour, grout and equipment must be present to ensure continuous placement.
4.6 Application - Gravity Flow.
    - Mixed grout should be poured one side of the void to avoid air entrapment. Grout is best poured over short distances to ensure this. Use a suitable header box, maintaining the grout head at all times to ensure continuous flow. To facilitate grout compaction and top plate contact, use rodding, tamping or flexible strapping in short strokes while maintaining an adequate head of grout. Do not vibrate as this will cause segregation. Any adjacent machinery or equipment causing vibration should be shut down until initial set (5-6 hrs). Pumping
    - When pumping SikaGrout-Deep Pour, ensure the pump is suitable for the grout consistency and for the distance and height it is to be pumped. A positive displacement pump is recommended.
    - Place grout by pumping into the farthest corner, filling the space gradually. Ensure that air is not entrapped under the base plate. Maximum aggregate size is 5mm. Ensure that selected pump is suitable for pumping this size of aggregate.
4.7 Curing treatment. Suitable curing methods such as plastic sheet, wet hessian, liquid membrane etc. must be used to protect the freshly applied grout from the drying effects of sun and wind. Curing must commence immediately after placement, and continue for at least 7 days. Curing is vital to the ultimate performance of grout as it allows optimum strength development and ensures tight contact with the baseplate.
4.8 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with water immediately after use. Hardened material can only be mechanically removed.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C minimum; +35 °C maximum
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5 °C minimum; +35 °C maximum
5.4 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Soluble chloride ion content: ≤ 0.05% (EN 1015-17)
    - Compressive strength: 1 day | ~ 12.0 MPa; 3 days | ~ 30.0 MPa; 7 days | ~ 50.0 MPa; 28 days | ~ 70.0 MPa (AS 1478.2:2005)
    - Splitting tensile strength: 28 days | ~ 5.0 MPa (AS 1012.10:2000)
    - Electrical resistivity: 7 days | ~ 14,000 Ω.cm; 28 days | ~ 39,000 Ω.cm; 56 days | ~ 53,000 Ω.cm; 90 days | ~ 64,000 Ω.cm (FM5-578)
    - Flowability: ~ 500 mm (Flow trough) (AS 1478.2:2005)
    - Setting time: Temperature | Initial Set | Final Set; 23ºC | ~ 4 hrs 40 mins | ~ 7 hrs 45 mins (AS 2350.4:2006)
5.5 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.6 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaGrout® Deep Pour, May 2024, Version 01.05, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/u/sikagrout-deep-pour.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SikaGrout Deep Pour, version 05/05/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/9/MSDS%20SikaGrout%20Deep%20Pour%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaGrout® Deep Pour, version 20/11/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/j/sds-sikagrout-deeppour.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
